finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the file 'secret' contains malicious content that could be interpreted as a command
finding.assumptions: The file 'secret' is writable by an attacker and contains malicious content.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported finding suggests that the file 'secret' could be used for OS command injection. However, the code only reads the content of the file into a string variable 'password' using the getline function. There is no indication that this content is ever used to execute a command. The code does not contain any system calls or command execution functions that could be exploited if the file content were malicious. Additionally, the file 'secret' is only read once during the initialization of the EmailSender class, and its content is not modified or used in any way that could lead to command injection.

finding.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
finding.trigger: If any recipient email contains malicious script tags
finding.assumptions: The recipients vector can be controlled by an attacker and contains malicious content.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code does not involve any web technologies or outputs that would be susceptible to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The email content is being constructed and sent via SMTP, not rendered in a web browser. Therefore, there is no risk of XSS in this context.

finding.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
finding.trigger: If the subject contains malicious script tags

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code does not involve any web technologies or outputs that would be susceptible to XSS.
